note: How the player's hand weapons look and sit. Issue #25: the pistol and rifle are Hyper3D models (assets/gear/,  metres, muzzle +Z) shown with its own textures (retint false). Models are CC0 (Kenney, via the MIT starter kit; see assets/third_party/kenney_starter_kit_fps/LICENSE.md) and are retinted at runtime so they read as worn gunmetal, not toys. 'emitter': false leaves off the glowing ring and core PlayerAvatar puts round the muzzle (the orange tip); the pistol and rifle have none, the muzzle flash still shows when firing. All transforms are chest space (+Z forward, +X the character's left). Grips and muzzle are in model space, before scale.

sights.note: Iron sights in model space: front post on the sight line, rear blade pair either side of it.

hold_3p.note: Issue #324: third person, the right fist on the pistol grip (as rifle_blaster's 'r'); the support hand is left as it is.

Issues #631, #324: third person, the right fist closed on the hilt (PlayerAvatar._seat_fist). 'one_hand': the left arm walks free. 'grip': the point on the sword the fist closes on (sword space, m). 'passes': re-aims of the arm until the skin's fist is on the grip. 'hands': each hand's grip for HandGrip (src/systems/look/hand_grip.gd): 'radius' m from the bar's axis to the finger bones (the hilt's 2 cm plus half a finger), 'curl' per finger [index, middle, ring, little], 'thumb' 'wrap' or 'along', 'max_deg' per joint [base, middle, tip].

plasma_welder.note: Issue #722: the plasma welder, the Hyper3D torch (assets/gear/plasma_welder.glb, content/look/gear_models.json) placed by model_xf, its tip at nozzle; held like the energy blade ('held_like': the blade's guard pose, its first person fist and its third person hold, copied below) with no swing. Simple shapes from WelderLook (src/systems/look/welder_look.gd), the nozzle up the blade's +Y; WelderFx (src/systems/look/welder_fx.gd) puts the sparks and the arc at the nozzle. 'tint': body, trim, tank, the nozzle's glow and the arc.

rest.note: Issue #722: how it hangs when not in use (chest space): the arm down by the side, the torch held low, the rod pointing ahead and down.

guard.note: Held out in front while welding (fire held, or a hold-E weld): the blade's guard, away from the body, the rod leaning forward to the work. Comes up from rest over the item's raise_s.

model_xf.note: Puts the torch's grip on the hilt's: its handle top (model 0.055, -0.099, -0.084) at the origin, tipped back 12 degrees about it and at 0.92, so the tip sits about half a metre in front of the face.

cut.note: Issue #229: boxes (model space) cut from the model's mesh: its own optic block, so only our scope shows, and the front sight post, which stood in the lowered scope's view.

scope.note: Procedural scope in model space: axis along +Z at pos, rear end (eyepiece) is the ads sight. Rings on mounts down to a rail at rail_y (the receiver top, once the model's own optic is cut).

aim.note: Third person: shouldered, the butt (pivot) in the right shoulder pocket; the gun turns about it to the crosshair. 'blade_deg': the chest turns this much more into the shot as the gun comes up (on top of the spine's own turn), so the left shoulder comes forward and the left hand reaches the handguard, as a real shooter stands; the gun turns back about its butt by the whole torso turn, and the head turns back too. The gun sits 3.5 cm further out, 14.5 cm lower and 1.6 cm further back than it first did, so the stock's top corner (model 0.012, 0.079, -0.455) is in the shoulder pocket and the stock rests in the shoulder rather than up beside the head; the troopers' rifles read this too (NpcBody._gun_aim_xf), and the sniper rifle copies it.

hold_3p.note: Issue #324: third person, both hands closed on the gun (PlayerAvatar._seat_hand, HandGrip). Each hand: 'grip' the point it closes on (rifle space, m; on the pistol grip and the handguard, not the kit's grips), 'bar' the grip's axis toward the thumb, 'palm' from the back of the hand toward the grip (rifle space), 'radius' m from the grip's axis to the finger bones, 'curl' per finger (the trigger finger lies along the guard), 'thumb' 'wrap' or 'along'.

sniper_rifle.note: The fence's sniper rifle: the rifle's own model, near black (dark), a longer barrel run out of its own (barrel, model space: the model's barrel is centred at y 0.048 and ends at z 0.475, so the tube starts inside it and a collar covers the joint), and a scope whose reticle is drawn on screen as a digital one with the range to the target (digital; PlayerWeapons). ads zoom_steps: right-click aims at the first, a second right-click goes to the next, one more puts it down.

hold_3p.note: Issue #324: third person, both hands closed on the gun (PlayerAvatar._seat_hand, HandGrip). Each hand: 'grip' the point it closes on (rifle space, m; on the pistol grip and the handguard, not the kit's grips), 'bar' the grip's axis toward the thumb, 'palm' from the back of the hand toward the grip (rifle space), 'radius' m from the grip's axis to the finger bones, 'curl' per finger (the trigger finger lies along the guard), 'thumb' 'wrap' or 'along'.

seeker_launcher.note: The seeker launcher: a plain tube with a scope, built from simple shapes (LauncherLook, src/systems/look/launcher_look.gd; 'build': 'launcher', no model), held over the right shoulder. Model space: the tube's axis along +Z, the origin on the axis where it sits on the shoulder; 'tube' its radius, its back and front ends (z) and the flared bells. A pistol grip under it for the right hand and a front grip for the left ('grips', the hands' IK targets; 'hold_3p' closes them on the grips as the rifle's). The sight is a square see-through display on a bracket off the tube's left side (scope 'panel', GunSights.build_panel): a dark frame round blue glass, its centre the ads sight, 'relief' in front of the eye. Aimed in, the glass tints the view and DigitalReticle draws its display on it (scan lines, rulers, status strips) with the sniper's crosshair and readouts (range, zoom) in 'reticle'; the lock box is SeekerLockView as before. The tube shows to the right of it at an angle, its top in view, running in from the edge of the view: the panel sits 12 cm left of the tube's axis and 7 cm over it, so the tube passes the eye outside the view and nothing of it is cut where you can see; 'barrel_from' only drops what is inside the camera's near plane (the player's tube is weapon_solid, LauncherLook 'viewmodel'). 'tex_scale': the favela's painted metal on the tube and trim, tiles a metre. 'aim': the tube on the right shoulder beside the head (chest space), turning about the shoulder contact (pivot) to the crosshair. 'aim_fpv': first person, lower and further right than the head so the tube runs in from the bottom right of the view with the panel on its left. 'carry' launcher: it stays on the shoulder at rest too (WeaponCarry REST/SPRINT 'launcher'). 'tint': tube, trim, grip.

reload_roll.note: The reload: the tube rolls about its own axis to the right (its top toward your right), off the shoulder and down a little, the muzzle up a touch (WeaponMotion.reload_roll_local); the right hand stays on its grip and the arm follows, the left goes to the back of the tube for the next round ('mag', 'reload_out') as before.

throw.note: Issue #372: the overarm grenade throw (src/systems/anim/throw_pose.gd). Hands in chest space, metres (+X the body's left, +Y up, +Z ahead; the right shoulder is at -0.22, 0.18, 0). Holding F the right hand waits at 'wind' (behind and above the shoulder, the grenade in it) and the left points ahead at 'left'. Letting go swings the right hand over 'over', through 'release' and down to 'follow' in swing_s seconds; the grenade leaves the hand release_at of the way through. The arms ease in and out over blend_s; the gun is tucked away while the hand is busy.

wheel.note: The Tab weapon wheel (issue #410). hold_time: seconds of Tab before it opens (shorter is a tap that cycles). dead_zone: fraction of the radius that is the middle. mouse_pixels: mouse travel from the middle to the rim. radius and inner are on-screen pixels.

muzzle_light.note: The flash's light. It sits `ahead` metres past the muzzle so the hand on the grip is lit warm, not blown out.

blade_volume.note: issue #16: the blade was too loud; dB for its one-shots and its hum
